items.title: A rational map from a reduced algebraic space to a separated one is represented by a morphism on its domain of definition
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors

items.difficulty_reason: Counts the author Lemma: for a rational map phi from a reduced algebraic space X to a separated algebraic space Y over S, there is a unique morphism f : U -> Y on the domain of definition U representing phi (source lines 9811-9818). The proof compares two representatives (V, g) and (V', g'), which agree on a dense open W contained in V intersect V'; the equalizer E of the two restrictions is a closed subspace because it is the base change of the diagonal of Y, and since W is contained in E while W is dense, |E| equals |V intersect V'|; reducedness then upgrades this to E = V intersect V' scheme theoretically, so the representatives glue along the fppf surjection from the disjoint union of the V to U.
